title: You’re not “standing your ground.”
paragraphs: You’re not “standing your ground.”
You might be resisting God.
And that’s more dangerous than you think.

Because sometimes the thing you’re protecting…
is the very thing God is asking you to lay down.
Here are 4 signs you’re defending what God wants you to surrender:

1. You keep justifying it instead of praying about it.
You’ve got reasons. Logic. Explanations.
But deep down—you haven’t brought it to God honestly.
Because you already know what He’ll say.
“And we know…” (Romans 8:28) — but we only quote that when it benefits us.

2. Correction feels like attack.
When someone speaks truth, you get defensive fast.
Walls go up. Tone changes.
Why? Because light is touching something you don’t want exposed.
“But whoever lives by the truth comes into the light…” (John 3:21)

3. You call it “peace” but it’s really avoidance.
You say, “I just want peace.”
But real peace doesn’t come from ignoring conviction.
It comes from surrender.
Jonah slept in the storm—
not because he had peace,
but because he was running.

4. Jesus isn’t Lord over that area.
Be honest.
You love Him… but not there.
Not that relationship.
Not that habit.
Not that secret.
“Why do you call me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ and do not do what I say?” (Luke 6:46)
But here’s what we miss…

God isn’t trying to take from you.
He’s trying to free you.

That thing you’re gripping so tightly?
It’s already costing you more than surrender ever will.
The cross proves it.

Jesus Christ didn’t defend His rights.
He surrendered them.

Not because He was weak—
but because love was stronger.

And through that surrender…
came your salvation.
So what are you still holding onto?

Pride?
Control?
A relationship God already warned you about?
A version of your life you refuse to release?
Let it go.

Not because it’s easy.
But because He’s worthy.

And because on the other side of surrender…
is freedom you’ve never tasted.

From hidden battles to holy freedom—
because Jesus rewrites everything.
